A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OTP research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite title edits and pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic optimal-transport and image-translation experiments in Section 5, plus ICNN experiments, noise-scheduling ablations and benchmark results in Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their numerical and qualitative outcomes in Section 5 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same source smoothing, decreasing noise schedule and alternating network updates. The distribution annotation added to v3 Eq. 21 restates the existing Gaussian smoothing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic scenarios, MNIST-to-CMNIST, Male-to-Female and Wild-to-Cat tasks, and the Appendix F.3 Wasserstein-2 benchmark.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: OTM/OTM-s in the synthetic comparisons, NOT/OTM/DIOTM/DSBM/ASBM in their respective image benchmarks, and the same baseline variants in Table 4.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain the same dimensions, image resolutions, metrics, evaluation samples, architectures, training budgets and noise schedules. No revised experimental protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Appendix F retains the same ICNN analysis, constant-versus-decreasing noise ablation and qualitative examples. The revised mathematical counterexample in Section 3.2.1 does not introduce an empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Experimental scores remain point estimates. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed details, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes OTM's One-to-Many Dtarget at d = 4 from 73.23 to 0.090 under unchanged reported settings. This places OTM slightly ahead of OTP's unchanged 0.094 on that metric. Other experimental values and qualitative results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Example 1 replaces the globally quadratic potential with one equal to negative infinity outside target support B, adds a c-concavity justification and derives the resulting support restriction in v3 Eqs. 12–14. It also corrects the transport cost from 2/3 to 1/3. The principal theorems and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about sufficient conditions, recovering deterministic and stochastic optimal transport, and image-translation performance. Replacing 'spurious' with 'fake' does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of mode collapse, noise scheduling and image-translation metrics remain unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning subsequence convergence and sufficient rather than necessary conditions.

D1.justification: Appendix E retains the same dataset-generation instructions, network descriptions, optimizer settings, batch sizes, iteration counts and noise-scheduling details. No new implementation or resource-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Appendix D research positioning are unchanged. The new Example 1 footnote invokes a theorem from the already-cited Santambrogio (2015), without adding a distinct work or revising novelty claims.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and running headers replace 'spurious' with 'fake', and the ICML proceedings notice becomes 'Preliminary work.' Local explanations expand, while nearly all prose and the section hierarchy remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 and Table 1 move from left to right columns, and the expanded Example 1 equations and footnote cause text reflow. All ten figures and four tables are retained; figure image contents and table structures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects Example 1's transport cost from 2/3 to 1/3 and supplies a support-restricted potential with an explicit derivation, improving that counterexample's rigor. The Table 1 revision reduces OTP's apparent advantage in one setting. These are localized improvements in precision; the core methodology, remaining evidence and limitations are unchanged.
